title: U3: two shortlist `likely_met` rows verified NOT met — and this PR is opened through pr-opener to settle BL-20260903
body:
**Tier-1** — registers only, one file, 6 insertions / 4 deletions. Lane: OPS, MI-279, unit **U3**.

⚠️ **This PR is itself the experiment.** It is opened **through `pr-opener.yml`** from a request file containing `"draft": false`, because that is the literal, and deliberately narrow, criterion of `BL-20260903-PR-OPENER-DRAFT-FALSE-IS-UNREACHABLE-SO-TIER-1-CAN-NEVER-SELF-LAND-THROUGH-THE-RELAY`:

> *A PR opened THROUGH pr-opener.yml from a request file containing `"draft": false` comes back `draft: false` on `pull_request_read` — read the PR's own draft field, never the workflow diff and never the request file. NOT sufficient: the jq expression being changed (that is the fix, not the observation); a unit test of the expression; or a PR opened by `create_pull_request` via the MCP, which never had this bug and would prove nothing.*

The code **is** fixed — `jq -r '.draft // false'` — but the row rules that out as evidence, correctly, since the failure class is a workflow that reads right and behaves otherwise. So the observation is produced rather than argued. **The outcome is not asserted anywhere in the diff**: the row records the METHOD, and whichever way this PR's `draft` field comes back is reported afterwards. If it is `true`, the fix is incomplete and that is the better finding.

## Two `likely_met` candidates, both verified NOT met

`scripts/ops/backlog_drain_candidates.py` shortlisted 6 rows as `likely_met`. I checked two and **neither is**, each for a reason worth writing down:

**`BL-20260816-NO-PER-ORDER-IB-CANCEL`** — matched on `path_added_since_filing: scripts/ops/cancel_ib_order.py`. That path existing is **criterion 2, which the row already marks SHIPPED**; criteria 4 and 5 are the open ones and the tool cannot see that.

But the check was not wasted: **criterion 4's stated blocker is cleared.** It records that at 12:37:33Z the IB breaker was open and the diag read returned `could_not_look`. At **2026-09-12T13:23:23Z it returns `read_state: orders_read`** with real rows — so the row moves from *blocked on an unavailable read* to *runnable, pending a Tier-2 dispatch*.

⚠️ **The live book offers one imperfect candidate and two excluded by construction:** MES `order_id 6` carries `client_id 9917` (above the 9000 execution band, so its owner resolves and `--force-client-id` would not bite) but it is OCA-grouped (`oca-protect-408`), so it is protective and needs `--force-protective`, and it already reads `PendingCancel` so it may stop being a test subject at any moment. MHG `634`/`635` carry `client_id 497` — the trader's own execution client, exactly the class criterion 5 says nothing outside the trader can cancel.

**I did not run it.** `cancel-ib-order` is Tier-2 and this lane routes Tier-2 to the manager as a proposal — including the dry run, since dispatching the action is the Tier-2 act whatever flag it carries.

**`BL-20260903`** — matched on `path_added_since_filing: .github/pr-landing/README.md`, a file with nothing to do with the jq expression.

## Why this is worth a diff

The drain skill says this tool *"shortlists; it never decides"* and records that its first version was **almost entirely wrong**. Both rows now carry a worked example of the exact signal that mis-matched them, so the next session does not close either on the same evidence.

## Verification

`backlog_append --check-live` OK · `check_backlog_refs --base origin/main` OK · `check_claim_basis` 0 findings · `register-field-loss` OK. Both rows amended through `update_row`, no hand splice.
